title: K8s deploy heuristics: baremetal-to-vSphere transition
body:
Purpose and scope:
This is a working heuristics doc for teams doing a greenfield or migration deployment of Kubernetes clusters across two common on-prem footprints: dedicated bare-metal racks and VMware vSphere pools. Focus: pragmatic preflight/postflight checks, Terraform module notes, and an operational upgrade strategy that minimizes downtime for inference serving workloads.

Audience:
- SREs and infra engineers running private deployments
- Solutions engineers validating customer on-prem requirements
- Platform engineers adapting Terraform modules for mixed fleets

Assumptions (explicit):
- Clusters are upstream Kubernetes (1.28+ recommended) with kubeadm or cluster-api-based lifecycle.
- Providers: metal nodes with iPXE/bootstrap or VMware vSphere (vCenter 7.0+).
- Networking: Calico or Cilium; BGP optional for bare-metal.
- Storage: local PVs for cache, CSI for persistent workloads (Longhorn or vSphere CSI).
- Customer can provide an out-of-band bastion and DNS control.

High-level phases (quick):
1) Preflight discovery and inventory
2) Provisioning (Terraform + bootstrap scripts)
3) Initial validation and smoke tests
4) Workload onboarding and soak
5) Controlled upgrades and rollback plan

Inventory & discovery checklist (pre-install, items to collect):
- vCenter FQDN/IP, datacenter, datastore names, cluster name, resource pool path, template/OVF names
- Bare-metal: BMC IPs, MAC addresses, iPXE config, remote console access, serial-over-LAN details
- Network: VLAN IDs, MTU, L3 gateway, BGP ASN (if used), egress NAT info for private registries
- Storage: list of SAN/NFS endpoints or vSphere datastore policies, CSI compatibility matrix
- Security: KMS/HSM endpoints, customer K8s RBAC policy constraints, allowed Egress URL list for images
- Operational: NTP servers, corporate CA certs, monitoring endpoints (Prometheus pushgateway or pull), log collectors

Preflight automated checks (scripts to run from an operations laptop or bastion):
- SSH and BMC access test: ssh root@<ip>; ipmitool -I lanplus -H <bmc> -U <user> sol info
- DNS resolution: dig +short <vcenter>, <registry>, <k8s-api-lb>
- Template/OS image checksum: sha256sum vsphere-template.ova
- Network MTU probe: ping -M do -s 8972 <target>
- Time sync: chronyc tracking or timedatectl status
- Disk health: smartctl -H /dev/sdX (bare-metal)

Terraform module notes (patterns & pitfalls):
- Keep provider blocks in a top-level module that chooses between vsphere and metal providers via a "provider_mode" variable.
- Module naming: module "compute_pool" should accept a "mode" var with values ["baremetal","vsphere"] and produce a unified output set: node_ips, node_names, ssh_user, provisioner_hooks
- Avoid encoding bootstrap scripts inline in Terraform resources. Instead, write bootstrap scripts to an artifact bucket or a file asset, reference via templatefile(). This makes diffs tractable and avoids huge plan outputs.
- Sensitive outputs: do NOT output private keys or kubeconfigs. If an operator needs kubeconfig, write to an S3/MinIO object with short TTL and record an object id as output.
- Recommended variables (minimal): cluster_name, region_tag, provider_mode, node_counts (controlplane, worker), vsphere_datastore, baremetal_profile_id, registry_mirror
- Example variable naming convention: "vm_template_name", "metal_profile_ilo_user". Keep provider-specific vars grouped under a map for clarity.
- State management: for mixed fleets, separate Terraform state files per provider to reduce blast radius (e.g., state-baremetal.tfstate, state-vsphere.tfstate).
- Idempotency: ensure that external actions (like OS image import) are guarded with data resources and null_resource triggers, not recreated every apply.

Bootstrap & provisioning heuristics:
- Bare-metal: prefer PXE+iPXE flows for automated installs. Keep a fallback manual : serial console and a preseed/cloudinit fallback image for emergency provisioning.
- vSphere: use resource pools + templates; use cloud-init or sysprep-equivalent. Avoid powering on directly into automatic kubeadm join steps until node registration is predictable.
- Image hygiene: build immutable golden images with required kernel tunables for hugepages, device-mapper, and iommu settings baked in. Use a nightly CI job for image builds and artifact promotion.

Initial validation & smoke tests (post-provision):
- Node readiness: kubectl get nodes --no-headers | awk '{print $2}' should show "Ready"
- CNI checks: verify pod-to-pod across nodes, run netshoot traceroutes between nodes, validate serviceClusterIP connectivity
- CSI: create a PVC, bind, write a file, and verify reading from another pod on a different node
- GPU checks (if applicable): nvidia-smi on host and inside container with --gpus=all; check driver-container compatibility
- KV cache and inference-specific checks: run a small inference job against a canary model; measure p95 latency and KV cache hit metrics

Upgrade strategy (control plane + node upgrades):
- Principles: one thing at a time, measurable, reversible. Aim for planned node-by-node upgrades with canary control plane when possible.
- Control plane: prefer rolling controller-manager/kube-apiserver upgrades using static pods or kubeadm upgrade plan. If using stacked etcd on controlplane nodes, upgrade etcd sequentially with snapshot and sanity checks after each node.
- Worker nodes: drain/workers one at a time with PodDisruptionBudgets respected for inference stateful workloads. Use rollout strategy: cordon->drain->update image->reboot->uncordon.
- Canary workloads: maintain a small dedicated worker pool for canaries; send 5–10% of traffic and validate latency/correctness before broader rollouts.

Rollback plan (quick bullets):
- Always take etcd snapshot before control-plane change: ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl snapshot save /tmp/etcd-snap.db --endpoints=<ep>
- If control plane fails, restore etcd snapshot into isolated restore cluster to validate snapshot integrity before full restore.
- For node upgrade failures, reprovision with previous golden image and rejoin cluster using token or kubeadm join --discovery-token-ca-cert-hash.

Post-upgrade validations (smoke):
- Run suite: node readiness, core DNS resolution for pods, basic inference canary, storage mount validation, cluster autoscaler sanity if used
- Compare perf baselines: p50/p95 token decode and model latency compared to pre-upgrade baseline; tag metrics with "upgrade_id" for correlation

Operational runbook snippets (copy-paste friendly):
- Drain & update node (example):
  kubectl cordon node-42
  kubectl drain node-42 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
  ssh admin@node-42 'sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y linux-image-... && sudo reboot'
  # wait for node to return, then
  kubectl uncordon node-42

- Snapshot etcd (example):
  export ETCDCTL_API=3
  etcdctl --endpoints=https://127.0.0.1:2379 --cert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/peer.crt --key=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/peer.key snapshot save /var/backups/etcd-$(date +%F).db

Testing & canary plan for inference services:
- Traffic split by routing proxy (NGINX/Envoy): add header X-Upgrade-Canary: true for 5% of requests
- Run A/B evaluation harness for 24 hours: compare token generation quality, latency, failure rate; auto-abort if error rate > 0.5% or p95 latency regresses > 30%

Notes on air-gapped environments: 
- Mirror registry images into local registry and pin image digests in manifests.
- Preload CRI-O/containerd images on nodes or use an init job to pull images from local registry.
- Keep a small HTTP artifact store for Terraform templates and bootstrap scripts reachable via corporate proxy.

Open questions / action items (work in progress):
- Decide preferred control-plane blueprint: kubeadm stacked vs. external etcd vs. CAPI (tradeoffs: operational complexity vs. provider compatibility).
- Standardize image signing and attestation for golden images.
- Define a lightweight rollback automation to restore etcd and reapply last-known-good manifests within SLA window.

Appendix: useful commands & references
- kubeadm upgrade plan
- kubectl get cs / kubectl get componentstatuses (deprecated but sometimes used for quick checks)
- ipmitool and racadm command snippets for BMC ops
- link to internal policy: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/Private+Deploy+SLA

Quick TODOs before this doc is final:
- Add explicit Terraform module examples (small code snippets) and a sample vars.tfvars for a mixed fleet
- Add a small CI test harness that validates the bootstrap flow end-to-end in a lab environment
- Author a postmortem template for failed upgrades to capture metrics and root cause quickly

Notes to self: keep this doc short and pragmatic. If something feels like "too much theory", try it in the lab and record the sequence that worked (commands, timings, race conditions).
